records.title: Dynamic Methylation Changes in Alzheimer’s Disease-Related Genes During Mindfulness Practice – a Proof-of-Concept Study
records.summary: In 17 long-term meditators and 17 matched controls, researchers examined methylation at 19 CpG sites across seven genes. A month-long retreat was associated with changes at selected sites, including ABCA7 and HOXA3; some ADAM10 differences separated meditators from controls.
records.limitation: A small, nonrandomized blood-methylation study. It did not measure brain RNA or establish prevention or treatment of Alzheimer’s disease. Baseline average ADAM10 methylation did not remain significant after multiple-testing correction.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Experienced meditators and matched controls were compared without random allocation.

topics.title: Mindfulness, DNA methylation and genetic variation

records.summary: In 24 people receiving EMDR or trauma-focused CBT for treatment-resistant depression, 148 microRNAs passed quality control. The combined sample’s miR-132-3p change survived correction for multiple testing.

records.title: Neural mechanisms of mindfulness: reduced neural reactivity to social-evaluative threat accounts for mindfulness intervention effects on inflammatory gene expression
records.authors: Blades RB, Boyle CC, Eisenberger NI, Cole SW, Korecki JRT, Fuligni AJ, Bower JE.
records.design: Randomized controlled trial; registered single-blind (outcome assessors)
records.summary: After six weeks, the meditation group showed lower neural responses to social-evaluative threat and lower inferred NF-κB activity. The gene-regulation difference lost statistical significance after adjustment for the neural-response change.
records.limitation: A small waitlist-controlled trial. Promoter analysis estimates transcription-factor activity; the analysis does not establish a causal neural mechanism.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The linked trial register specifies masked outcome assessors; participants knew their allocation.

records.title: Oxidative stress-induced proinflammatory secretion from retinal pigment epithelium disrupts NAD+ metabolism via CD38 on macrophages leading to immune microenvironment dysregulation
records.authors: Lin R, Liang F, Hu C, Jiang L, Wan Z, Xu Z, Luo Y, Ma J, Wu Y, Cai W, Yu J.
records.summary: Oxidatively damaged retinal pigment epithelium altered macrophage transcription and NAD+ metabolism. CD38 upregulation and inhibitor experiments implicated a CD38/NAD+ pathway.
records.limitation: This is oxidative-injury pathway research. It does not establish a visual-exposure effect or a human treatment benefit.

records.title: Shared Transcriptomic and Epigenomic Signatures Between Traumatic Brain Injury and Music Exposure: An Integrative Proof of Concept
records.authors: Gómez-Carballa A, Pischedda S, Mallah NEZ, Nowak W, Martinón-Torres F, Navarro L, Salas A.
records.summary: The analysis identified overlapping molecular signatures between music-exposure datasets and traumatic-brain-injury datasets, including 154 shared differentially expressed genes.
records.limitation: Music was not administered to the brain-injury cohorts in this comparison. Shared signatures do not demonstrate a treatment effect.

evidence.text: Shared Transcriptomic and Epigenomic Signatures Between Traumatic Brain Injury and Music Exposure: An Integrative Proof of Concept

records.authors: Cavenaghi A, Mallah NEZ, Navarro L, Martinón-Torres F, Gómez-Carballa A, Salas A.
records.summary: The pilot detected exploratory RNA and microbial changes after music exposure, including signals involving HERC6, TSPAN5 and REM2.

records.authors: Berbegal-Sáez P, Gallego-Landin I, Macía J, Valverde O.

records.title: Psychological assessments, allostatic load and gene expression analyses in a randomized controlled trial comparing meditation, yoga, and stress education
records.authors: Denninger JW, Joss D, Romero PM, Khalsa SBS, Hoge EA, Bhasin M, Lazar SW, Dusek JA, Macklin E, Libermann T, Fricchione GL, Benson H.
records.design: Randomized controlled trial; registered double-blind (participants and outcome assessors)
records.summary: The three-arm trial found no significant between-group effects on psychological, genomic or allostatic-load outcomes. Most psychological measures improved within each group. Circulating IL-6 increased slightly within the meditation group at follow-up, remaining in the normal range.
records.limitation: Within-group improvement does not establish a treatment advantage. Participants were stressed but otherwise healthy; results may differ in clinical populations.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The linked trial register specifies double masking of participants and outcome assessors. The article does not describe the masking procedure; this classification reflects the registered design.

records.title: Effect of a Web-Based Heartfulness Program on the Mental Well-Being, Biomarkers, and Gene Expression Profile of Health Care Students: Randomized Controlled Trial
records.authors: Thimmapuram J, Patel KD, Bhatt D, Chauhan A, Madhusudhan D, Bhatt KK, Deshpande S, Budhbhatti U, Joshi C.
records.design: Randomized controlled trial; blinding not reported
records.summary: At 12 weeks, RNA sequencing identified 292 upregulated and 1,180 downregulated genes in the meditation group relative to controls. Reported stress and distress improved. IL-6 protein fell in both groups, with a larger reduction in controls.
records.limitation: An exploratory trial with an inactive comparator and exclusion of participants missing follow-up. Enrichment analysis does not establish changes in every gene belonging to a pathway.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The article and ISRCTN record describe random allocation but do not report blinding. Blinding is not established by these sources.

records.title: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction Reduces Proinflammatory Gene Regulation But Not Systemic Inflammation Among Older Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial
records.authors: Lindsay EK, Marsland AL, Cole SW, Dutcher JM, Greco CM, Wright AGC, Brown KW, Creswell JD.
records.summary: MBSR reduced inferred NF-κB activity relative to the active comparison programme (d=0.17; p=0.028). It did not reduce circulating IL-6 or C-reactive protein. CREB, IRF and glucocorticoid-receptor pathway differences were not statistically significant.
records.limitation: The gene-regulation signal was small and did not translate into a measured reduction in systemic inflammation. Pathway activity was inferred from RNA profiles.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Laboratory technicians were blind to treatment condition; the linked trial register identifies single masking of outcome assessors.

records.title: Predicting psychosocial intervention response from baseline gene expression
records.authors: Ricon-Becker I, West TN, Fredrickson BL, Kaplan DM, Mehl MR, Raison CL, Cole SW.
records.design: Prediction analyses across two randomized trials
records.summary: Baseline CREB activity predicted selected psychological responses to compassion-based meditation in two datasets. The same relationship was not seen for mindfulness meditation.
records.limitation: The study concerns prediction from baseline expression rather than a demonstrated therapy-induced transcriptional mechanism. Clinical deployment requires further validation.

records.title: Serotonin Transporter (SLC6A4) and FK506-Binding Protein 5 (FKBP5) Genotype and Methylation Relationships with Response to Meditation in Veterans with PTSD
records.authors: Lee A, Thuras P, Baller J, Jiao C, Guo B, Erbes CR, Polusny MA, Liu C, Wu B, Lim KO, Bishop JR.
records.design: Secondary analysis of two intervention studies
records.summary: SLC6A4 genotype was associated with symptom improvement among veterans exposed to early-life trauma. Change in a group of nine FKBP5 methylation sites was associated with greater improvement (OR 2.8; 95% CI 1.1–7.1).
records.limitation: Genotype and DNA methylation were measured; this is not direct RNA-expression evidence. Associations across two meditation studies do not isolate a treatment mechanism.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The reported analysis relates genotype and methylation to response across two studies; it is not an independent blinded randomized treatment comparison.

records.authors: Zhang Z, Wu Y, Zhou S, Fu P, Yan H.
records.summary: Music and white-noise exposures produced different immune-related, microbial and oxidative-stress profiles in mice.
records.limitation: Animal exposure conditions do not establish a human music benefit. Gene assays, microbial composition and serum enzyme activity are distinct outcomes.

records.authors: Anna Bludau; Uwe Schwartz; Daniela M. Zeitler; Melanie Royer; Gunter Meister; Inga D. Neumann; Rohit Menon
records.summary: Septal miR-132 contributed to social-fear extinction and oxytocin-mediated reversal of social fear in male mice. Manipulation in oxytocin-receptor-expressing neurons linked this microRNA to behavioural responses and downstream Gdf5 regulation.

records.authors: Liu W, Zhu X, Ge X, Chen Y, Li DW, Gong L.
records.summary: Strong light exposure induced retinal inflammatory transcriptional changes. Vitreous IL-6 protein was approximately tenfold higher in the injury model.

records.title: Music compensates for altered gene expression in age-related cognitive disorders
records.authors: Gómez-Carballa A, Navarro L, Pardo-Seco J, Bello X, Pischedda S, Viz-Lasheras S, Camino-Mera A, Currás MJ, Ferreirós I, Mallah N, Rey-Vázquez S, Redondo L, Dacosta-Urbieta A, Caamaño-Viña F, Rivero-Calle I, Rodriguez-Tenreiro C, Martinón-Torres F, Salas A.
records.summary: A music session was associated with blood gene-expression changes in people with age-related cognitive disorders and healthy controls. Some affected pathways overlapped inversely with disease-associated expression patterns.
records.limitation: Before–after molecular associations and cross-dataset comparisons do not establish that music reverses dementia or changes brain gene expression.

records.authors: Rosana Carvalho Silva; Vincenzo Dattilo; Giulia Perusi; Monica Mazzelli; Elisabetta Maffioletti; Roberta Bazzanella; Marco Bortolomasi; Annamaria Cattaneo; Massimo Gennarelli; Alessandra Minelli
records.summary: In 21 people receiving EMDR or trauma-focused CBT for treatment-resistant depression, whole-blood NR3C1, FKBP5 and SGK1 expression varied over time. FKBP5 and SGK1 fell significantly at eight weeks; transcript levels rebounded during follow-up.

records.title: Epigenetic impact of a 1-week intensive multimodal group program for adolescents with multiple adverse childhood experiences.
records.authors: Kaliman P, Cosín-Tomás M, Madrid A, Roque López S, Llanez-Anaya E, Papale LA, Alisch RS, Davidson RJ.
records.summary: A one-week programme combining mindfulness, artistic expression and EMDR group therapy studied 44 adolescent girls with multiple adverse experiences. Forty-nine DNA-methylation loci differed with intervention; SIRT5 and TRAPPC2L changes correlated with trauma measures.
records.limitation: The programme has several components. Saliva methylation findings do not isolate EMDR; the study detected no intervention effect on intrinsic epigenetic age acceleration.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The methods report random-number allocation for 44 girls. Post-allocation participant or assessor masking is not established. The intervention combines mindfulness, art and group EMDR.

records.limitation: A small trial of brief online practice in otherwise healthy nurses. The result concerns this dose and delivery; it does not establish the absence of effects from other programmes.

records.title: Quantitative cellular-resolution map of the oxytocin receptor in postnatally developing mouse brains
records.authors: Kyra T. Newmaster; Zachary T. Nolan; Uree Chon; Daniel J. Vanselow; Abigael R. Weit; Manal Tabbaa; Shizu Hidema; Katsuhiko Nishimori; Elizabeth A. D. Hammock; Yongsoo Kim
records.summary: Cellular-resolution maps show that oxytocin receptor expression changes across brain regions and postnatal development in mice. records.authors: Quintana DS, Rokicki J, van der Meer D, Alnæs D, Kaufmann T, Córdova-Palomera A, Dieset I, Andreassen OA, Westlye LT.
records.design: Human post-mortem expression mapping and co-expression analysis
quotes: “Three oxytocin signaling genes have been frequently implicated in human social behavior: OXT (structural gene for oxytocin), OXTR (oxytocin receptor), and CD38 (oxytocin secretion).”

“Expression of the three selected oxytocin pathway genes was enriched in subcortical and olfactory regions and there was high co-expression with several dopaminergic and muscarinic acetylcholine genes, reflecting an anatomical basis for critical gene pathway interactions.”
“The oxytocin signaling system may interact with dopaminergic and muscarinic acetylcholine signaling to modulate cognitive state processes involved in complex human behaviors.”
records.summary: Human brain expression maps showed regional enrichment of oxytocin-pathway transcripts and co-expression with dopaminergic and muscarinic acetylcholine genes. The study provides anatomical context for an OXTR-centred research programme.
records.limitation: Spatial co-expression is an association. This study did not test sound, vision or language interventions, Fibonacci-derived features, or causal interactions across the proposed target network.

records.title: Mindfulness meditation for younger breast cancer survivors: A randomized controlled trial
records.authors: Bower JE, Crosswell AD, Stanton AL, Crespi CM, Winston D, Arevalo J, Ma J, Cole SW, Ganz PA.
records.design: Randomized controlled trial; blinding not reported
quotes: “A brief, mindfulness‐based intervention demonstrated preliminary short‐term efficacy in reducing stress, behavioral symptoms, and proinflammatory signaling in younger breast cancer survivors”
“women in the mindfulness group who practiced more frequently did evidence lower levels of IL‐6 at the post‐treatment assessment”

“our trial indicates that the benefits of mindfulness may extend to genomic markers of inflammation, including reductions in proinflammatory gene expression and activity of the proinflammatory transcription factor NF‐ κ B”
records.summary: Meditation reduced perceived stress and proinflammatory gene expression after treatment. Depression improvement was not statistically significant. Most psychological and behavioural benefits were not maintained at three months.
records.limitation: A preliminary waitlist-controlled trial in a specific survivor population. Molecular changes do not establish a reduction in cancer recurrence or progression.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The published methods describe randomization to mindfulness or waitlist but do not report masked outcome assessment.

records.title: Oxytocin receptor gene (OXTR) is related to psychological resources
records.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
records.authors: Saphire-Bernstein S, Way BM, Kim HS, Sherman DK, Taylor SE.
quotes: “Psychological resources—optimism, mastery, and self-esteem—buffer the deleterious effects of stress and are predictors of neurophysiological and psychological health-related outcomes. These resources have been shown to be highly heritable, yet the genetic basis for this heritability remains unknown.”

“Here, we report a link between the oxytocin receptor (OXTR) SNP rs53576 and psychological resources, such that carriers of the “A” allele have lower levels of optimism, mastery, and self-esteem, relative to G/G homozygotes.”

“OXTR was also associated with depressive symptomatology. Mediation analysis indicates that the effects of OXTR on depressive symptoms may be largely mediated by the influence of OXTR on psychological resources.”

records.title: Electromagnetic detection of HIV DNA in the blood of AIDS patients treated by antiretroviral therapy
records.authors: Montagnier L, Aïssa J, Lavallée C, Mbamy M, Varon J, Chenal H.
quotes: “Electromagnetic signals of low frequency have been shown to be durably produced in aqueous dilutions of the Human Immunodeficiency Virus DNA.
In vivo, HIV DNA signals are detected only in patients previously treated by antiretroviral therapy and having no detectable viral RNA copies in their blood.

We suggest that the treatment of AIDS patients pushes the virus towards a new mode of replication implying only DNA, thus forming a reservoir insensitive to retroviral inhibitors. Implications for new approaches aimed at eradicating HIV infection are discussed.”

records.title: Epigenetic regulation of the glucocorticoid receptor in human brain associates with childhood abuse
records.authors: Patrick O McGowan; Aya Sasaki; Ana C D'Alessio; Sergiy Dymov; Benoit Labonté; Moshe Szyf; Gustavo Turecki; Michael J Meaney
records.design: Human postmortem observational study and laboratory assays
records.summary: Hippocampal tissue from suicide victims with a history of childhood abuse showed altered glucocorticoid-receptor promoter methylation and lower receptor transcript levels. Laboratory promoter assays supported a potential regulatory link between methylation and transcription.
records.limitation: Postmortem associations cannot establish that childhood adversity caused the molecular differences or that the pattern applies to every exposed person.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Human postmortem observational study and laboratory assays. No masked human randomized trial classification is assigned.

records.title: Interaction effect of oxytocin receptor (OXTR) rs53576 genotype and maternal postpartum depression on child behavioural problems
quotes: “The results revealed a significant effect in the interaction between OXTR rs53576 genotype and maternal postpartum depression on externalising problems in children with AA genotype ( β = 0.136, 95% CI 0.032 to 0.240), but not in those with GG/GA genotype.”

“This indicates that an interaction of vulnerable genotypes (i.e., A allele of OXTR rs53576) with an environmental burden (i.e. maternal postpartum depression) may be one of the potential elements that predisposes the infant to developing behavioural problems early in life.”
“Hence, special attention needs to be paid to children exposed to environmental risks such as maternal postpartum depression, to facilitate the provision of appropriate care.”

records.title: Quantum annealing versus classical machine learning applied to a simplified computational biology problem
quotes: “Transcription factors regulate gene expression, but how these proteins recognize and specifically bind to their DNA targets is still debated. Machine learning models are effective means to reveal interaction mechanisms. Here we studied the ability of a quantum machine learning approach to classify and rank binding affinities.”

“Despite technological limitations, we find a slight advantage in classification performance and nearly equal ranking performance using the quantum annealer for these fairly small training data sets.”
“Thus, we propose that quantum annealing might be an effective method to implement machine learning for certain computational biology problems.

topics.title: Quantum computing methods for bioinformatics and gene-expression modelling

records.title: Timewave Zero - I Ching fractal map of time
records.journal: Terrance McKenna, Dennis McKenna and Peter Meyer
quotes: “The principal device of the Timewave Zero theory is a fractal function (constructed using numerical values derived from the King Wen Sequence of I Ching hexagrams) which maps time onto 'novelty'.”

“the "revealed" axiom that all phenomena are at root constellated by a wave form which is the hierarchical summation of its constituent parts, morphogenetic patterns related to those in DNA. ... quotes: “In particular, it is immediately recognized the observed relevance of extremely low signal (ELS) in the phenomena under study. records.title: Bacterial gene regulatory neural network as a biocomputing library of mathematical solvers
records.authors: Adrian Ratwatte; Samitha Somathilaka; Ngoc Dan Thanh Cao; Xu Li; Sasitharan Balasubramaniam
records.design: Transcriptomic data analysis and gene-network computational modelling
records.summary: A search procedure identifies bacterial regulatory subnetworks whose expression responses match several finite mathematical tasks. One output-gene pattern approximates Fibonacci numbers across a small set of chemically encoded conditions.
records.limitation: Subnetworks are selected for agreement with the target pattern. The finite input set and computational stability analyses do not establish unrestricted arithmetic, natural selection for Fibonacci computation, or performance on unseen tasks.

records.title: Community singing intervention reduces maternal salivary cytokines and enhances maternal-infant cortisol synchrony in postnatal depression: biological findings from the SHAPER-PND trial
records.authors: Kirkpatrick M, Priestley K, Bind RH, Rebecchini L, Borsini A, Estevao C, Hazelgrove K, Laijawala R, Alford S, Woods AJ, Crane N, Manoharan M, Burton A, Dye H, Osborn T, Greenwood L, Dazzan P, Fancourt D, Pariante C.
records.design: Biomarker analysis within a randomized trial
records.summary: After the first community-singing session, salivary IL-6 decreased by 26% in the singing group. The time-by-group interaction for IL-6 was significant. Later analyses also examined mother–infant cortisol synchrony and communication.
records.limitation: This measured salivary cytokine protein, not IL6 transcription. The biological subset was unbalanced, and speech correlations do not isolate the causal effect of particular words.

records.authors: Ryohei Nemoto; Xiangzhi Meng; Behzad Mortezapour; Alexander Weismann; Saya Nakano; Masahisa Tsuchiizu; Ryuichi Arafune; Noriaki Takagi; Sho Nakamura; Katsunori Wakabayashi; Rie Suizu; Richard Berndt; Takashi Uchihashi; Kunio Awaga
records.summary: The authors assembled a molecular diatomic kagome lattice and observed electronic states along its zigzag edges. Microscopy and calculations connect these states to the lattice's electronic structure and topology.
records.limitation: This is a quantum-materials result, not a demonstration of a longer-lived qubit or an error-correcting computer. It provides an example of geometry changing electronic behaviour, without establishing a Fibonacci mechanism.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Molecular-lattice microscopy and tight-binding calculations. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

records.authors: Fernández-Álvarez C, Mosteiro-Díaz MP, Zuazua-Rico D, Maestro-González A.

records.authors: Fan H, Zhang J, Wang Y, Yang K, Wang Y, Yang X.
records.summary: Ninety-five university students were randomized to peer-delivered EMD plus imagery rescripting, imagery rescripting alone or care as usual. records.title: Surface code scaling on heavy-hex superconducting quantum processors
records.authors: Arian Vezvaee; Cesar Benito; Mario Morford-Oberst; Alejandro Bermudez; Daniel A. Lidar
records.summary: The authors combine surface-code layouts and pulse control on IBM heavy-hex processors. Increasing code size along one direction improves protection of particular logical states. Their analysis shows why both state directions and coherent noise matter when assessing error suppression.
records.limitation: Directional improvements do not establish general below-threshold scaling. The paper identifies further noise reduction needed for balanced scaling. It does not test Fibonacci or M9 P24 sequences.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Superconducting quantum-processor experiment and modelling. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

records.authors: Wojciech Bożejko; Mariusz Uchroński; Mieczysław Wodecki
records.design: Combinatorial construction and quantum-annealing computational experiment
records.summary: The authors construct a permutation neighbourhood with Fibonacci-number cardinality and encode it using a binary sequence of length n−1. They test a related QUBO formulation on a D-Wave system for a single-machine scheduling problem.

records.title: Theta binaural beats for pain, cognition and anxiety
records.summary: Across 13 RCTs, theta (4-8 Hz) binaural beats reduced pain, showed anxiety benefit mainly in procedural and chronic-pain settings, and improved episodic memory—supporting focused testing in Universal Mind's 5-8 Hz range.
records.limitation: Overall pain evidence was low certainty, outcomes varied, and the review does not establish PTSD efficacy or validate a complete sound layer.

records.title: Effectiveness of an intensive outpatient treatment programme combining prolonged exposure and EMDR therapy for adolescents and young adults with PTSD in a naturalistic setting.
records.authors: Rentinck EM, van Mourik R, de Jongh A, Matthijssen SJMA.
records.summary: A six-day programme combining prolonged exposure, EMDR, physical activity and support from relatives or friends included 74 people aged 12–25. At one month, 65% no longer met PTSD criteria; dropout was 4%.
records.limitation: Intensive clinician-delivered, multimodal treatment with no randomized comparator. The sample included 36 people aged 12–17 and 38 aged 18–25; it does not establish a gentle entertainment effect.

records.title: Fibonacci-modulation-induced multiple topological Anderson insulators
records.authors: Ruijiang Ji; Zhihao Xu
records.summary: A one-dimensional spin-orbit-coupled chain with Fibonacci modulation exhibits multiple modelled topological Anderson-insulator phases and multifractal wave functions as parameters vary.
records.limitation: The paper proposes a cold-atom realization; the modelled phases are not reported as an experimental observation. The result remains specific to the chosen Hamiltonian and modulation.

records.title: Heat-rechargeable computation in DNA logic circuits and neural networks
records.authors: Tianqi Song; Lulu Qian
records.summary: Heat resets engineered DNA circuits for repeated computation. A feedforward logic circuit returns the first 16 Fibonacci-word elements from index inputs and maintains performance across 16 computation rounds with 15 resets.
records.limitation: The Fibonacci circuit uses a designed truth table and finite inputs. It does not autonomously generate an unbounded sequence or reveal a naturally occurring genomic computation.

records.authors: Barnhofer T, Dunn BD, Strauss C, Ruths FA, Barrett B, Ryan M, Ladwa A, Stafford F, Fichera R, Baber H, McGuinness A, Metcalfe I, Kan DKY, Pooley J, Harding D, Tassie E, Carson J, Rhodes S, Young AH, Connors J, Warren FC.

records.authors: Hoppen TH, Wessarges L, Jehn M, Mutz J, Kip A, Schlechter P, Meiser-Stedman R, Morina N.
records.summary: Across 70 pediatric PTSD trials involving 5,528 participants, EMDR reduced symptoms relative to passive controls at treatment end (g = 0.86). Trauma-focused CBT had the most consistent evidence across time points.
records.limitation: The 70 trials cover several therapies, not EMDR alone. Longer-term EMDR data remain limited; included ages extend to 19.

records.title: Realizing string-net condensation: Fibonacci anyon braiding for universal gates and sampling chromatic polynomials
records.authors: Zlatko K. Minev; Khadijeh Najafi; Swarnadeep Majumder; Juven Wang; Ady Stern; Eun-Ah Kim; Chao-Ming Jian; Guanyu Zhu
records.summary: The authors construct Fibonacci string-net states with a dynamical preparation method, measure and braid anyons, and estimate chromatic polynomials for several graphs using quantum samples.
records.limitation: The experiments are proof of principle with error mitigation. The authors identify noise and comparison with classical approximation algorithms as unresolved barriers to a demonstrated quantum advantage.

records.title: Brain wave modulation and EEG power changes during auditory beats stimulation
records.authors: Dos Anjos T, Di Rienzo F, Benoit CE, Daligault S, Guillot A.
records.summary: In 28 healthy participants, four minutes of isochronic-derived stimulation produced greater gamma-band EEG power changes than gamma binaural beats and white noise, alongside a distinct time-related alpha response.
records.limitation: The stimulus alternated audible frequencies rather than using a conventional fixed-carrier isochronic tone and did not test Universal Mind's exact protocol. It measured short-term EEG responses, not a clinical outcome.

topics.title: Brain entrainment, pain, anxiety and heart-rate variability

records.title: Effects of intranasal oxytocin on fear extinction learning
records.authors: Mahmoud Rashidi; Joe J. Simon; Katja Bertsch; Gerhard Vincent Wegen; Beate Ditzen; Herta Flor; Valery Grinevich; Robert Christian Wolf; Sabine C. Herpertz
records.summary: In 124 healthy women, intranasal oxytocin impaired fear-extinction learning relative to placebo. The result challenges the assumption that oxytocin uniformly improves extinction and highlights the importance of timing and experimental context.
records.limitation: Healthy participants completed a laboratory conditioning task. The trial did not test a clinical PTSD treatment or measure gene expression.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The article reports a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled human experiment. Its outcome is laboratory fear extinction.

records.title: Enhancing detection of topological order by local error correction
records.authors: Iris Cong; Nishad Maskara; Minh C. Tran; Hannes Pichler; Giulia Semeghini; Susanne F. Yelin; Soonwon Choi; Mikhail D. Lukin
records.design: Numerical modelling and analysis of Rydberg-atom measurements
records.summary: Cong and colleagues use local error-correction ideas to identify topological order despite noise. They test the method numerically and apply it to measurements from a Rydberg-atom quantum spin liquid, making it directly relevant to analysing neutral-atom experiments.
records.limitation: The method improves the diagnosis of a prepared state. It is not a demonstration that Aquila stores arbitrary information fault-tolerantly, and it does not test M9 P24 sequences.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Numerical modelling and analysis of Rydberg-atom measurements. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

records.title: Enhancing image security via chaotic maps, Fibonacci, Tribonacci transformations, and DWT diffusion: a robust data encryption approach
records.authors: Mohammad Mazyad Hazzazi; Mujeeb Ur Rehman; Arslan Shafique; Amer Aljaedi; Zaid Bassfar; Aminu Bello Usman
records.summary: The proposed grayscale-image encryption pipeline combines chaotic keys, Fibonacci pixel permutation, Tribonacci transformations, bit-plane operations and wavelet-based diffusion. The paper reports statistical and timing tests.
records.limitation: Entropy, pixel correlation and timing tests do not alone establish cryptographic security. The multi-component pipeline also prevents attributing its reported performance solely to Fibonacci transforms.

records.title: The Penrose Tiling is a Quantum Error-Correcting Code
records.authors: Zhi Li; Latham Boyle
records.summary: Li and Boyle construct quantum error-correcting codes from Penrose tilings and variants based on Ammann–Beenker and Fibonacci tilings. Their construction connects nonperiodic geometric structure with the ability to recover information after local errors or erasures.
records.limitation: This is a mathematical construction in a preprint, not an experimental demonstration on Aquila. Its Fibonacci tilings are different from the Atlas M9 P24 sequences. A physical implementation and its resource requirements remain separate questions.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Theoretical preprint; version 2. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

records.authors: Daniel L. Bowling
records.summary: The authors organise music and mental-health research around biological principles involving reward, rhythm, learning and social connection. records.limitation: A broad mechanistic review; it does not supply one pooled treatment effect or establish that every music intervention acts through the same pathways.

records.title: Light disrupts social memory via a retina-to-supraoptic nucleus circuit
records.authors: Huang YF, Liao PY, Yu JH, Chen SK.
records.summary: Acute light exposure impaired social-recognition memory through a retinal pathway that inhibited supraoptic oxytocin neurons. Experimental activation of these neurons altered the behavioural response.
records.limitation: Neural activity and behavioural changes are separate from OXTR gene expression. The animal circuit findings do not validate a human visual intervention.

records.limitation: This result applies to a structured, teacher-led MBSR course and the trial’s noninferiority margin. It is not a test of an app or gene expression.

records.title: Dynamical topological phase realized in a trapped-ion quantum simulator
records.authors: Philipp T. Dumitrescu; Justin G. Bohnet; John P. Gaebler; Aaron Hankin; David Hayes; Ajesh Kumar; Brian Neyenhuis; Romain Vasseur; Andrew C. Potter
records.summary: A quasiperiodic Fibonacci drive creates a dynamical topological phase in a ten-qubit trapped-ion chain. Edge-qubit behaviour exhibits protection against specified control imperfections relative to a periodic-drive comparison.
records.limitation: The result concerns a finite quantum simulator and particular dynamics. It does not demonstrate general-purpose fault tolerance; the present appraisal covers the abstract and accessible extended-data descriptions.

chapterEntries.summary: A quasiperiodic Fibonacci drive creates a dynamical topological phase in a ten-qubit trapped-ion chain. Edge-qubit behaviour exhibits protection against specified control imperfections relative to a periodic-drive comparison.
chapterEntries.limitation: The result concerns a finite quantum simulator and particular dynamics. It does not demonstrate general-purpose fault tolerance; the present appraisal covers the abstract and accessible extended-data descriptions.

records.authors: Leen NA, de Weijer AD, van Rooij SJH, Kennis M, Baas JMP, Geuze E.
records.summary: Plasma anandamide and 2-AG were measured in 54 veterans with PTSD and 26 combat controls. Pretreatment levels did not predict symptom reduction following trauma-focused therapy; cortisol decreased over time.

records.authors: Kazuaki Amikura; Hiroshi Ito; Miho S. Kitazawa
records.design: Plant morphology measurements and mathematical model
records.summary: Rose stems show a non-random distribution of prickles relative to spiral leaf phyllotaxis. A diffusion-based inhibition model reproduces the measured pattern and selected patterns in other plants.
records.limitation: The primary measurements cover nine shoots of one rose cultivar. The model assumes a patterning process; the responsible inhibitory factors and broader applicability remain unresolved.

records.title: Dynamically Generated Logical Qubits
records.authors: Matthew B. Hastings; Jeongwan Haah
records.summary: Hastings and Haah construct a honeycomb code in which a repeating schedule of two-qubit measurements creates logical qubits. Information protection comes from the code and measurement sequence acting together on the lattice.
records.limitation: The paper does not show that a passive hexagon alone protects information. Implementing this code requires the specified measurements and decoding; the current Aquila workflow does not implement that procedure.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Theoretical quantum error-correcting code. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

records.title: The IBM Quantum heavy hex lattice
records.authors: Paul Nation; Hanhee Paik; Andrew Cross; Zaira Nazario
records.summary: IBM explains why its heavy-hex architecture uses a sparse pattern of superconducting-qubit connections. The design reduces frequency collisions and unwanted effects on neighbouring qubits while balancing connectivity and the operations required by a calculation.
records.limitation: This is a vendor technical explanation, not a peer-reviewed Fibonacci study. Its benefits depend on superconducting hardware and control choices; the shape alone is not evidence of universal quantum stability.

records.title: Effects of extremely low-frequency electromagnetic fields on B16F10 cancer cells
records.authors: Tang JY, Yeh TW, Huang YT, Wang MH, Jang LS.
quotes: “The results yielded a 17% inhibition rate under 7.83 Hz compared with that of the control group.
Moreover, sweep frequencies in narrow intervals (7.83 ± 0.1 Hz for the step 0.05 Hz) caused an inhibition rate of 26.4%, and inhibitory effects decreased as frequency sweep intervals increased.
These results indicate that a Schumann resonance frequency of 7.83 Hz can inhibit the growth of cancer cells and that using a specific frequency type can lead to more effective growth inhibition.”

records.title: Gamification Use and Design in Popular Health and Fitness Mobile Applications
records.journal: American journal of health promotion : AJHP
records.authors: Cotton V, Patel MS.
quotes: “Gamification was commonly used by popular health and fitness mobile applications, but none used the specified behavioral economic principles to design rewards or points. Mobile applications could potentially improve their use if their design better leveraged principles from behavioral economic”

“Use of behavioral economic principles focused on designing rewards or points using loss aversion (allocated upfront and could be lost), variable reinforcement (not allocated constantly), and probability inflation (using drawings or lottery designs).”

“The top 50 rankes free health and fitness apps were downloaded from the App Store by Apple. Gamification was used by 64% of mobile applications. Most applications that included gamification (97%) targeted behaviors related to physical activity and weight loss. Applications focused on other areas such as reproductive health, meditation, and sleep used gamification less often (11%). Game elements used most commonly included goal setting (78%), social influences (78%), and challenges (63%), while less common elements included points (6%) and levels (3%). No applications incorporated behavioral economics principles specified in the study.”

records.title: Effect of 528 Hz Music on the Endocrine System and Autonomic Nervous System
quotes: “ In the 528 Hz condition , mean levels of cortisol significantly decreased , chromogranin A tended to decrease , and oxytocin doubled after only 5 minutes of music exposure . However, no significant change was observed in any salivary biomarkers in the 440 Hz condition.”

The influence of music on the autonomic nervous system and endocrine system varies depending on the frequency of the music, and furthermore, that 528 Hz music has an especially strong stress-reducing effect , even following only five minutes of exposure .”
records.summary: After five minutes of 528 Hz music, mean salivary oxytocin rose from 37.57 to 73.58 and cortisol later fell from 0.43 to 0.25; neither change was significant with 440 Hz music.
records.limitation: Only nine healthy adults participated. The short comparison is intriguing biomarker evidence, not clinical proof, and requires larger independent preregistered replication.

records.title: Hexadirectional coding of visual space in human entorhinal cortex
records.authors: Matthias Nau; Tobias Navarro Schröder; Jacob L. S. Bellmund; Christian F. Doeller
records.design: Human fMRI during controlled visual tracking
records.summary: Nau and colleagues found a sixfold directional pattern in human entorhinal-cortex activity during a visual tracking task. The result supports a grid-like representation of visual space and gives Vision Atlas a measured example of sixfold organisation in brain activity.
records.limitation: An fMRI population signal is not a direct image of individual grid cells or proof of a tetrahedral eye mechanism. This study does not test Fibonacci sequences, EMDR outcomes, or quantum error correction.

records.title: Social stress induces neurovascular pathology promoting depression
records.authors: Caroline Menard; Madeline L. Pfau; Georgia E. Hodes; Veronika Kana; Victoria X. Wang; Sylvain Bouchard; Aki Takahashi; Meghan E. Flanigan; Hossein Aleyasin; Katherine B. LeClair; William G. Janssen; Benoit Labonté; Eric M. Parise; Zachary S. Lorsch; Sam A. Golden; Mitra Heshmati; Carol Tamminga; Gustavo Turecki; Matthew Campbell; Zahi A. Fayad; Cheuk Ying Tang; Miriam Merad; Scott J. Russo
records.design: Experimental mouse study with human postmortem comparison
records.summary: Chronic social stress reduced the tight-junction protein claudin-5 in susceptible mice, increasing blood–brain barrier permeability and allowing peripheral IL-6 into the brain. Reduced CLDN5 was also observed in postmortem tissue from people with depression.
records.limitation: Causal manipulations were performed in mice. IL-6 infiltration is a protein-level finding; the human comparison is observational.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Experimental mouse study with human postmortem comparison. No masked human randomized trial classification is assigned.

quotes: “The use of binaural beat technology in the theta brainwave frequency embedded into music decreases physical and psychological indications of stress. Binaural beat technology embedded with beta and delta frequencies may improve cognitive functioning and sleep quality, respectively.”

records.title: Towards an understanding of spiral patterning in the Sargassum muticum shoot apex
records.authors: Marina Linardić; Siobhan A. Braybrook
records.design: Algal developmental observations and perturbation experiments
records.summary: Sargassum muticum displays a mean divergence angle close to the golden angle. Organ placement is uncoupled from apical-cell division orientation, while the tested auxin and wall-softening explanations fail to account for bud position.
records.limitation: The developmental signal remains unidentified. Similar geometry in algae and plants does not establish a shared molecular mechanism.

records.limitation: The biological observations come from earlier studies. Constant-angle development and a fitness advantage for uniform spacing are model assumptions; a controlled evolutionary test is absent.

records.title: Two-dimensional Fibonacci grating for far-field super-resolution imaging
records.authors: Kedi Wu; Guo Ping Wang
records.summary: A two-dimensional Fibonacci grating is designed to convert evanescent information into propagating light. Analytical calculations and numerical simulations predict far-field reconstruction beyond a wavelength divided by seven in the tested configuration.
records.limitation: The reported imaging resolution is a simulated result. Fabrication tolerance, experimental noise and performance on biological specimens are not established by these calculations.

records.summary: An energy-cost model identifies the golden angle as an optimum for transitions between phyllotactic fractions and reproduces several common and less common leaf-arrangement sequences.
records.limitation: The proposed evolutionary explanation depends on the chosen transition-cost model. Agreement with known patterns does not measure the assumed energy costs or establish the genetic mechanism.

records.authors: Polusny MA, Erbes CR, Thuras P, Moran A, Lamberty GJ, Collins RC, Rodman JL, Lim KO.
records.summary: MBSR produced greater improvement in self-reported PTSD symptoms than present-centred therapy. More participants achieved clinically significant symptom improvement, but loss of PTSD diagnosis did not differ significantly.
records.limitation: The mean advantage was modest, and treatment-session duration differed between groups. This study did not measure gene expression.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The publication and authors’ follow-up confirm blinded clinical interviews. Participants knew their treatment. The register labels investigators and assessors as double masked; this classification follows the confirmed assessor blinding in the published study.

records.title: A healthy heart is not a metronome: an integrative review of the heart's anatomy and heart rate variability
records.authors: Shaffer F, McCraty R, Zerr CL.
quotes: “Physiological coherence is used broadly and includes all of the specific approaches for quantifying the various types of coherence measures, such as cross-coherence (frequency entrainment between respiration, BP, and heart rhythms), or synchronization among systems (e.g., synchronization between various EEG rhythms and the cardiac cycle), auto-coherence (stability of a single waveform such as respiration or HRV patterns), and system resonance.”

“A coherent heart rhythm is defined as a relatively harmonic (sine-wave-like) signal with a very narrow, high-amplitude peak in the LF region of the HRV power spectrum with no major peaks in the VLF or HF regions. Coherence is assessed by identifying the maximum peak in the 0.04–0.26 Hz range of the HRV power spectrum, calculating the integral in a window 0.030 Hz wide, centered on the highest peak in that region, and then calculating the total power of the entire spectrum. The coherence ratio is formulated as: (Peak Power/[Total Power – Peak Power])”

“With practice, people can learn to breathe at their cardiovascular system's resonance frequency. This aligns the three oscillators (baroreflex, HR, and BP) at that frequency and moves the peak frequency from the HF range (≈0.2 Hz) to the LF range (≈0.1 Hz). Breathing at the resonance frequency more than doubles the energy in the LF band (0.04–0.15 Hz). This corresponds to the Institute of HeartMath's heart rhythm coherence, which is associated with a “narrow, high-amplitude, easily visualized peak” from 0.09 to 0.14 Hz”

“The resonance frequency model uses the mechanism of slow breathing at an individual’s resonance frequency, while the psychological coherence model adds and emphasizes the importance of the pattern and stability of vagal afferent traffic as important components of emotional self-regulation. Both approaches have been associated with increased overall HRV over time.”

“There is agreement that the concept of “coherence” in the heart rate signal is observed as a peak in the HRV power spectrum around 0.1 Hz, which reflects resonance frequency of breathing and resonance in the baroreflex. The authors’ “psychophysiological coherence model” advocates biofeedback training that actually creates a maximum of HRV variability at this virtual single frequency.”

“It is known that the power spectrum distribution of normal fluctuations in a healthy heart follows an 1/f pattern, characteristic of fractal signals. So, this leads us to juxtapose Coherence and simplicity vs fractals and complexity.”

records.authors: McConnell PA, Froeliger B, Garland EL, Ives JC, Sforzo GA.
quotes: “Acute exposure to theta-frequency binaural beats in a young, healthy sample of college students resulted in increased parasympathetic activation, increased sympathetic withdrawal, and increased self-reported relaxation post-exercise.”

records.title: Giving peace a chance: Oxytocin increases empathy to pain in the context of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict
records.authors: Shamay-Tsoory SG, Abu-Akel A, Palgi S, Sulieman R, Fischer-Shofty M, Levkovitz Y, Decety J.
quotes: “Israeli Jewish participants were asked to report their empathy to the pain of in-group (Jewish), neutral out-group (European), and adversary out-group (Palestinian) members.
“Oxytocin remarkably increased empathy to the pain of Palestinians, attenuating the effect of in-group empathy bias observed under the placebo condition.”

“This effect, we argue, is driven by the general role of oxytocin in increasing the salience of social agents which, in turn, may interfere with processes pertaining to derogation of out-group members during intractable conflicts.”

records.title: Social reward requires coordinated activity of nucleus accumbens oxytocin and serotonin
records.authors: Gül Dölen; Ayeh Darvishzadeh; Kee Wui Huang; Robert C. Malenka
records.summary: In mice, social reward required coordinated oxytocin and serotonin signalling in the nucleus accumbens. Removing oxytocin receptors from dorsal raphe inputs, or blocking accumbens serotonin 5-HT1B receptors, prevented the rewarding effect of social interaction.
records.limitation: The experiments identify a mouse neural mechanism. They do not measure SLC6A4 gene expression or test a human therapy.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Experimental mouse study. No masked human randomized trial classification is assigned.

records.title: Local stabilizer codes in three dimensions without string logical operators
records.authors: Jeongwan Haah
records.summary: Haah constructs local stabilizer codes in three dimensions without string-like logical operators. The work introduces a different geometric organisation of information and errors, associated with the fractal structure of logical operations in the cubic-code family.
records.limitation: This is code theory, not evidence that any fractal pattern stabilises a physical quantum computer. It does not demonstrate a Fibonacci connection or a complete self-correcting memory operating at finite temperature.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Theoretical three-dimensional stabilizer codes. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

records.title: Retinal origin of orientation maps in visual cortex
records.authors: Se-Bum Paik; Dario L Ringach
records.design: Computational model with comparative visual-cortex observations
records.summary: Paik and Ringach propose that interference between regularly spaced ON- and OFF-centre retinal ganglion-cell mosaics helps form orientation maps in visual cortex. Their model predicts hexagonal organisation of orientation-domain centres, with supporting patterns reported in four mammalian species.
records.limitation: This is a proposed developmental mechanism with supporting observations. It does not establish that all visual cortex follows this model, that humans prefer hexagons, or that retinal geometry stabilises quantum information.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Computational model with comparative visual-cortex observations. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

records.design: Plant developmental experiments and mechanistic model
records.summary: Experiments link polar auxin transport to the positions of new plant organs. Existing primordia act as auxin sinks, helping define the spacing and stability of phyllotactic patterns.

records.title: Baroreflex and oscillation of heart period at 0.1 Hz studied by α ‐blockade and cross‐spectral analysis in healthy humans
records.authors: Cevese A, Gulli G, Polati E, Gottin L, Grasso R.
quotes: “Here we address the question as to whether the low frequency variability ( ∼ 0.1 Hz) of the heart period may depend on a baroreflex‐mediated response to blood pressure oscillations, induced by the α ‐sympathetic drive on the peripheral resistance.”

“We conclude that in supine rest conditions, the oscillation of RR at low frequency is almost entirely accounted for by a baroreflex mechanism, since it is not produced in the absence of a 0.1 Hz pressure oscillation.”

“The results provide physiological support for the use of non‐invasive estimates of the closed‐loop baroreflex gain from cross‐spectral analysis of blood pressure and heart period variability in the 0.1 Hz range.”

records.title: The photoreceptor mosaic
records.authors: P K Ahnelt
records.design: Anatomical review of the human retinal photoreceptor mosaic
records.summary: Ahnelt describes how human rods and cones are distributed across the retina. Cone packing is especially dense near the fovea; different cone populations have different arrangements. This provides biological context for exploring local packing and sampling geometry in Vision Atlas.
records.limitation: The review does not demonstrate a universal perfect hexagonal retina, tetrahedral visual processing, or a Fibonacci mechanism. It is anatomical evidence, not an EMDR treatment trial or a quantum-stability experiment.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Anatomical review of the human retinal photoreceptor mosaic. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

records.title: 45 Days in a Greek Refugee Camp
quotes: “She explained her mother had met the Iraqi DJ just as he came out of the boat. “I wasn’t in the camp at the time but later, every volunteer was talking about how amazing this man was. He came the whole way from Turkey listening to his music on his huge headphones and, while he was at Platanos, he showed the songs to some volunteers.”

“Some seven days later, on the night of New Year’s Eve, Gabriela made her way to the registration camp. “While we were doing some work there, the DJ from Iraq stopped my mom because he remembered her. I was in the middle of Moria and this man put his headphones on my ears.”

“I started listening to an absolutely amazing remix of “Hello” by Adele, that he made. I couldn’t stop smiling and I almost started crying. Now, I think a lot about how I would like to hear that again.”

records.title: Congo dance project helps refugees take steps towards rebuilding lives
quotes: “Congolese choreographer Fabrice Don de Dieu Bwabulamutima believes in the healing power of dance.”

“He travels with his drama and dance company to refugee camps across the Democratic Republic of the Congo, teaching people who have experienced war and violence how to overcome trauma, rebuild their self-confidence and learn to live with other people again through the medium of dance.”

“Dance touches everybody, regardless of your position of power, your age or your race,” says the 40-year-old instructor who has put his own dance career on hold. His company, Kongo Drama, has been conducting a four-month dance, drama and music programme entitled ‘Refugees on the Move’ in Inke camp, in Nord-Ubangi province, which hosts more than 16,000 refugees from the Central African Republic.”

records.title: Dancing with Refugees - Expressing Feelings and Experiences
quotes: “Through dance, I can express experiences that I would not be able to verbalize in any other way. The possibility of using dance to say something about oneself, one’s own feelings and views is not to be found in traditional dance, which was what I learnt first. Rather, it is contemporary dance that makes that possible.”

“But in the workshops I feel it is important to start with tradition in order to show the participants that dance has something to do with them. It is part of their culture and can also become a means through which they can express themselves.”

“Dancing together brings them into the present, it creates a specific moment. That may be the starting point for actively shaping the future. Through reviving the culture the refugees feel they have lost, we lead them to a new way of dealing with it. It is as if we were opening up the possibility of a retrospective view, but one that focuses on what was beautiful and not on the suffering.”

records.title: Music & Refugees: Improving Lives In Uncertain Times
quotes: “Every other Saturday, LHI would put on a festival of events and activities, headlined by a Yazidi talent show. Every time, there were at least two or three musical performances, mainstays of a tradition that brought together culture and community to fill the void created by daily refugee life.”

“It’s amazing to see the difference between those who do and don’t have access to those kinds of classes,” Katelyn says. “They feel like they accomplished something...it’s almost therapeutic [for them] to even have a schedule.”

“For many refugees, the classes are far more than just a creative outlet. Most asylum seekers are fleeing from some sort of war or conflict. Many of them have lost family members and loved ones. As victims of ethnic genocide, many of the Yazidis in Serres experienced unimaginable trauma. And unfortunately, as Katelyn tells me, the traumatic events do not always stop with the arrival at a refugee camp.”

records.title: Refugees’ Stories Through Song: No Borders Music
quotes: “Elijah Gentle, a Melbourne-based advocate for displaced people, believes that music is an ideal vehicle for raising awareness and has established a project that documents the experiences of refugees in Eastern Europe through their own songs.”

“The name of this project is No Borders Music, and in it Gentle has recorded the music-making he encountered in refugee camps that he visited in Bosnia, Serbia, Macedonia, Greece and Lebanon. His aim it to combine these recordings with instrumentation prepared back in Australia, and thereby create a cross-cultural synthesis that embraces hip-hop, traditional Arabic music, Sufi, and East-West fusions.”
“Along with an audio album that will be released later this year, a documentary filmed by a Danish film maker is being made. A GoFundMe campaign to raise funds to cover costs is underway”

quotes: “Five patients with a major depressive episode (DSM-IV) underwent an acute 10 Hz rTMS challenge with 3000 stimuli over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex during an IBZM-SPECT bolus and constant infusion protocol.
Data of nine SPECT investigations showed a significant reduction by 9.6 ± 6.2% in IBZM binding to striatal dopamine D2 receptors after rTMS challenge compared to baseline.
